		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 8pt">

			<a href="#TableOfContents"><font style="display: inline;font-size:8pt;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">Customer</font><font style="display: inline;"> relationships assets relate primarily to underlying customer relationships. The preliminary estimated fair value of the customer relationships represents the sum of the present value of the expected cash flows attributable to those customer relationships. The cash flows were determined from the revenue and profit forecasts associated with growth opportunities that are expected to be generated from these customer relationships. The Company used the same method to determine the fair value of this intangible asset as the developed technologies and utilized a discount rate of </font><font style="display: inline;">16%</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:18pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Goodwill</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s primary reasons for the Acquisition was to accelerate the Company&#x2019;s time-to-market with early product leadership and a robust design win pipeline, including wins spanning tier one Data Center, original equipment manufacturer (OEM), and solid-state drive (SSD) customers.&nbsp; The Acquisition also enhanced the Company&#x2019;s engineering team through the addition of research and development resources.&nbsp; These factors were the basis for the recognition of goodwill. The goodwill is expected to be deductible for tax purposes over </font><font style="display: inline;">15</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.&nbsp;&nbsp;The acquired goodwill was allocated to our Enterprise Storage Products market segment. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:18pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Proforma disclosures</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The </font><font style="display: inline;">results</font><font style="display: inline;"> of operations of the Acquisition have been included in PMC&#x2019;s consolidated results of operations since the acquisition date.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The Acquisition did not have a significant impact on PMC&#x2019;s net revenues or net income (loss) for the periods where pro forma disclosures would be required.&nbsp; Net revenues for 2013 from the Acquisition date were </font><font style="display: inline;">$4.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and increased our net loss for the same period was </font><font style="display: inline;">$2.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million.&nbsp; Included in net loss was </font><font style="display: inline;">$4.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million related to amortization of purchased intangible assets, </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of fair value adjustments on acquired inventory, and </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of payroll accruals.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">NOTE 3. DERIVATIVE INSTRUMENTS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company generates revenues in U.S. dollars but incurs a portion of its operating expenses in various foreign currencies, primarily the Canadian dollar. To minimize the short-term impact of foreign currency fluctuations on the Company&#x2019;s operating expenses, the Company uses forward currency contracts.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Forward currency contracts that are used to hedge exposures to variability in forecasted foreign currency cash flows are designated as cash flow hedges. The maturities of these instruments are less than twelve months. For these derivatives, the gain or loss from the effective portion of the hedge is initially reported as a component of other comprehensive income in stockholders&#x2019; equity and subsequently reclassified to earnings in the same period in which the hedged transaction affects earnings. As the hedge transactions are incurred, the effective portion of the hedge is recognized into operating income. The gain or loss from the ineffective portion of the hedge is recognized as income or expense immediately.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At </font><font style="display: inline;">December</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;2</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">, the Company had </font><font style="display: inline;">150</font><font style="display: inline;"> foreign currency forward exchange contracts outstanding that qualified and were designated as cash flow hedges. At December&nbsp;28, 2013, there were </font><font style="display: inline;">27</font><font style="display: inline;"> such currency forward contracts outstanding. The U.S. dollar notional amount of these contracts was </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">40.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $</font><font style="display: inline;">27.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million at December&nbsp;2</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;"> and December&nbsp;2</font><font style="display: inline;">8</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively, and the contracts had a </font><font style="display: inline;">fair value of $</font><font style="display: inline;">1.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million loss</font><font style="display: inline;"> and a fair value of $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million </font><font style="display: inline;">loss</font><font style="display: inline;"> in December&nbsp;2</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;"> and December&nbsp;2</font><font style="display: inline;">8</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> respectively. </font><font style="display: inline;">No</font><font style="display: inline;"> portion of the hedging instrument&#x2019;s gain or loss was excluded from the assessment of effectiveness. The ineffective portions of hedges had no significant impact on earnings, nor are they expected to over the next twelve months.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">NOTE 4. FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENTS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:5pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">ASC Topic 820 specifies a hierarchy of valuation techniques which requires an entity to maximize the use of observable inputs that may be used to measure fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;The hierarchy is prioritized into three levels (with Level 3 being the lowest) defined as follows:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10.05pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 1: Inputs are based on quoted market prices for identical assets and liabilities in active markets at the measurement date. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10.05pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 2: Inputs include similar quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities; or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data for substantially the full term of the assets or liabilities. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10.05pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Level 3: Pricing inputs include significant inputs that are generally not observable in the marketplace. These inputs may be used with internally developed methodologies that result in management&#x2019;s best estimate of fair value. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:10.05pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s valuation techniques used to measure the fair value of money market funds and other financial instruments were derived from quoted prices in active markets for identical assets. The valuation techniques used to measure the fair value of all other financial instruments, all of which have counterparties with high credit ratings, were valued based on quoted market prices or model driven valuations using significant inputs derived from or corroborated by observable market data.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 8pt">

			<font style="display: inline;font-size:8pt;">53</font>

		</p>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:18pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Assets/Liabilities Measured and Recorded at Fair Value on a Non-Recurring Basis</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company measures the fair value of its indebtedness carried at amortized cost only for the purposes of disclosing such amounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 28, 2013, the carrying value of </font><font style="display: inline;">$30.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million outstanding drawdown on the Company&#x2019;s line of credit approximated its fair value, given the short-term nature of this borrowing and a lack of significant interest rate changes since the borrowing occurred.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;">non</font><font style="display: inline;">-financial assets, such as prepaid expenses and other current assets, property and equipment, and intangible assets are recorded at fair value only if an impairment charge is recognized.&nbsp;&nbsp;During 2014, 2013 and 2012, charges of $0.8 million, $3.0 million and $1.8 million, respectively, were recorded to fully write off certain assets that became impaired during those years. As their resulting carrying value was $nil, no further fair value measurements were necessary.&nbsp;&nbsp;The </font><font style="display: inline;">losses</font><font style="display: inline;"> recorded during 2014, 2013 and 2012 were mainly included in Research and Development expenses, net in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;See Note 1. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies for details on the asset impairments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The </font><font style="display: inline;">Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;"> estimates of expected volatilities are based on a weighted historical and market-based implied volatility. The Company uses historical data to estimate option exercises and employee terminations within the valuation model. Separate groups of employees that have similar historical exercise behavior are considered separately for valuation purposes. The expected term of options granted is derived from the output of the stock option valuation model and represents the period of time that granted options are expected to be outstanding. The risk-free rate for periods within the contractual life of the stock option is based on the U.S. Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of the grant.</font>

		<p style="margin:18pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Stock Option Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company issues its common stock under the provisions of the 2008 Equity Plan (the &#x201C;2008 Plan&#x201D;). Stock option awards are granted with an exercise price equal to the closing market price of the Company&#x2019;s common stock at the grant date. The options generally expire within </font><font style="display: inline;">10</font><font style="display: inline;"> years and vest over </font><font style="display: inline;">four</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The 2008 </font><font style="display: inline;">Plan</font><font style="display: inline;"> was approved by stockholders at the 2008 Annual Meeting.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2008 Plan became effective on January 1, 2009 (the &#x201C;Effective Date&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;It is a successor to the 1994 Incentive Stock Plan (the &#x201C;1994 Plan&#x201D;) and the 2001 Stock Option Plan (the &#x201C;2001 Plan&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Up to </font><font style="display: inline;">30,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of our common stock have been initially reserved for issuance under the 2008 Plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;At the 2012 Annual Meeting, stockholders approved an increase in shares reserved for issuance under the 2008 plan by </font><font style="display: inline;">9,500,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares which shares were registered on May 14, 2012 on Form S-8 bringing the total number of authorized and registered shares available under the 2008 Plan to </font><font style="display: inline;">39,500,000</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent that a share that is subject to an award that counts as </font><font style="display: inline;">1.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares against the 2008 Plan&#x2019;s share reserve is added back into the 2008 Plan upon expiration or termination of the award or repurchase or forfeiture of the shares, the number of shares of common stock available for issuance under the 2008 Plan will be credited with 1.6 shares.&nbsp;&nbsp;The implementation of the 2008 Plan did not affect any options or restricted stock units outstanding under the 1994 Plan or the 2001 Plan on the Effective Date.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent that any of those options or restricted stock units subsequently terminate unexercised or prior to issuance of shares thereunder, the number of shares of common stock subject to those terminated awards will be added to the share reserve available for issuance under the 2008 Plan, up to an additional </font><font style="display: inline;">15,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares. </font><font style="display: inline;">No</font><font style="display: inline;"> additional shares may be issued under the 1994 Plan or the </font><font style="display: inline;">2001</font><font style="display: inline;"> Plan.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">Restricted Stock Units</font><br /><font style="display: inline;"></font><br /><font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 36pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;">On February&nbsp;1, 2007, the Company amended its stock award plans to allow for the issuance of RSUs to employees and directors. The first grant of RSUs occurred on May&nbsp;25, 2007. The grants vest over varying terms, to a maximum of four years from the date of grant.&nbsp; On May 10, 2012, PMC stockholders approved the business criteria on which performance goals may be based so that awards granted may constitute performance-based compensation under Section 162(m) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the &#x201C;Code&#x201D;). &nbsp;On August 27, 2012 the Compensation Committee awarded the CEO the first performance RSU grant with a performance goal of the revenue target in the Company&#x2019;s 2012 internal operating plan.&nbsp; On January 22, 2013, the Compensation Committee certified the degree of achievement of the Company&#x2019;s 2012 revenue target and the number of earned RSUs to be released to the CEO; 50% of the earned RSUs were released on May 25, 2013, 25% of the earned RSUs were released on May 25, 2014 and 25% of the earned RSUs will be released on May 25, 2015. The total estimated </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million fair value of this 2012 grant based on the achievement of performance against target was and will be recognized as compensation expense over the grant&#x2019;s vesting terms, with </font><font style="display: inline;">50%</font><font style="display: inline;"> vesting on May 25, 2013, </font><font style="display: inline;">25%</font><font style="display: inline;"> vesting on May 25, 2014, and </font><font style="display: inline;">25%</font><font style="display: inline;"> vesting on May 25, 2015.</font>

		<p style="margin:18pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On August 26, 2013, performance RSUs were granted to the CEO and other Executives (&#x201C;Executive(s)&#x201D;) with a performance goal of the degree of achievement of Total Shareholder Return (&#x201C;TSR&#x201D;) relative to Global Industry Classification Standards (&#x201C;GICS&#x201D;) Semiconductor Companies (8-Digit) for the performance period (July 1,&nbsp; 2013 - June 30, 2015). Performance against the performance goal is anticipated to be reviewed on or about August 25, 2015 and earned RSUs will release 50% upon certification and 50% on August 25, 2016.&nbsp; The total estimated </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million fair value of these 2013 grants was and will be recognized as compensation expense over the grant&#x2019;s vesting terms, with </font><font style="display: inline;">50%</font><font style="display: inline;"> vesting on August 25, 2015 and </font><font style="display: inline;">50%</font><font style="display: inline;"> vesting on August 25, 2016. </font>

The goal of the performance-based RSU award under one program is the degree of achievement of TSR relative to GICS Semiconductor Companies (8-Digit) for the performance period (July 1,&nbsp;2014 - June 30, 2016). The total estimated </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million fair value of these 2014 awards was and will be recognized as compensation expense over the award&#x2019;s vesting terms, with </font><font style="display: inline;">50%</font><font style="display: inline;"> vesting on August 25, 2016 and </font><font style="display: inline;">50%</font><font style="display: inline;"> vesting on August 25, 2017. The goal of the performance-based RSU award under the second program is based on revenue or the Non-GAAP operating income target for each year in the Company&#x2019;s internal 2014-2016 operating plan. 			<font style="display: inline;">Employee Stock Purchase Plan</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The 2011 Employee Stock Purchase Plan (the &#x201C;2011 Plan&#x201D;) was approved by stockholders at the 2010 Annual Meeting.&nbsp; The 2011 Plan became effective on February 11, 2011. The 2011 Plan consists of consecutive offering periods, generally of a duration of 6 months, and allows eligible employees to purchase shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock at the end of each such offering period, generally February and August of any year, at a price per share equal to 85% of the lower of the fair market value of a share of Common Stock on the start date or the fair market value of a share of Common Stock on the exercise date of the offering period.&nbsp; Employees purchase such shares through payroll deductions which may not exceed 10% of their total cash compensation.&nbsp; The 2011 Plan imposes certain limitations upon an employee&#x2019;s right to acquire Common Stock, including the following: (i)&nbsp;no employee may purchase more than </font><font style="display: inline;">7,500</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;shares of Common Stock on any one purchase date and (ii)&nbsp;no employee may be granted rights to purchase more than </font><font style="display: inline;">$25,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> worth of Common Stock for each calendar year that such rights are at any time outstanding. &nbsp;Up to </font><font style="display: inline;">12,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of our Common Stock have been initially reserved for issuance under the 2011 Plan.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During 2014, </font><font style="display: inline;">1,916,727</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares were issued under the 2011 Plan at a weighted-average price of $</font><font style="display: inline;">5.66</font><font style="display: inline;"> per share. As of December&nbsp;27, 2014, </font><font style="display: inline;">4,380,208</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares were available for future issuance under the 2011 Plan (2013 - </font><font style="display: inline;">6,296,935</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares</font><font style="display: inline;"> available for issuance).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The weighted-average estimated fair values of Employee Stock Purchase Plan awards during years 2014, 2013, and 2012 were $</font><font style="display: inline;">1.74</font><font style="display: inline;">, $</font><font style="display: inline;">1.61</font><font style="display: inline;">, and $</font><font style="display: inline;">1.69</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">NOTE 11. SPECIAL SHARES</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At December&nbsp;27, 2014 and December&nbsp;28, 2013, the Company maintained a reserve of </font><font style="display: inline;">278,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">1,019,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares, respectively, of PMC common stock to be issued to holders of PMC-Sierra, Ltd. (&#x201C;LTD&#x201D;) special shares.&nbsp;&nbsp;During 2014, the Company amended its special shares registry to reflect cancellations, expirations, and conversions of LTD special shares, resulting in a reduction of </font><font style="display: inline;">734,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> special shares outstanding.&nbsp;&nbsp;The special shares of LTD, the Company&#x2019;s principal Canadian subsidiary, are redeemable or exchangeable for PMC common stock at certain conversion ratios. Special shares do not vote on matters presented to the Company&#x2019;s stockholders, but in all other respects represent the economic and functional equivalent of PMC common stock for which they can be redeemed or exchanged at the option of the holders. The special shares have class voting rights with respect to transactions that affect the rights of the special shares as a class and for certain extraordinary corporate transactions involving LTD. If LTD files for bankruptcy, is liquidated or dissolved,&nbsp;the special shares&nbsp;receive as a preference the number of shares of PMC&nbsp;common stock issuable on conversion plus a nominal amount per share plus unpaid dividends, or at the holder&#x2019;s option convert into&nbsp;LTD ordinary&nbsp;shares, which are the</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:7.5pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">functional&nbsp;equivalent of&nbsp;voting common stock. If the Company files for bankruptcy,&nbsp;is liquidated, or dissolved,&nbsp;special shares of LTD receive the cash equivalent of the value of&nbsp;PMC&nbsp;common stock into which the&nbsp;special&nbsp;shares could be converted, plus unpaid dividends, or at the holder&#x2019;s option convert into&nbsp;LTD ordinary&nbsp;shares. If&nbsp;the Company materially breaches&nbsp;its obligations to&nbsp;special&nbsp;shareholders of LTD (primarily to permit conversion of&nbsp;special&nbsp;shares into PMC common stock), the&nbsp;special&nbsp;shareholders may convert their shares into LTD ordinary shares.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">These special shares of LTD are classified outside of stockholders&#x2019; equity until such shares are exchanged for PMC common stock. Upon exchange, amounts will be transferred from the LTD special shares account to the Company&#x2019;s common stock and additional paid-in capital on the consolidated balance sheet.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">NOTE 12. STOCKHOLDERS&#x2019; EQUITY</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Authorized Capital Stock of PMC</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">At December&nbsp;27, 2014 and December&nbsp;28, 2013, the Company had an authorized capital of </font><font style="display: inline;">905,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares, </font><font style="display: inline;">900,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> of which are designated &#x201C;Common Stock&#x201D;, $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.001</font><font style="display: inline;"> par value, and </font><font style="display: inline;">5,000,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> of which are designated &#x201C;Preferred Stock&#x201D;, $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.001</font><font style="display: inline;"> par value.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:18pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Stock Repurchase Program</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During 2014, the Company repurchased </font><font style="display: inline;">1.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million shares of PMC common stock for a total of </font><font style="display: inline;">$8.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million. The Company acquired these common shares as part of its $275.0 million stock repurchase program announced on March 13, 2012.&nbsp; The repurchased shares were retired immediately upon delivery. Accordingly, the repurchased shares were recorded as a reduction of common stock, additional paid-in capital and accumulated deficit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During 2013, the Company repurchased </font><font style="display: inline;">13</font><font style="display: inline;"> million shares of PMC common stock for a total of </font><font style="display: inline;">$79.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million. The Company acquired these common shares as part of its $275.0 million stock repurchase program announced on March 13, 2012.&nbsp; The repurchased shares were retired immediately upon delivery. Accordingly, the repurchased shares were recorded as a reduction of common stock, additional paid-in capital and accumulated deficit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On May 2, 2012, the Company entered into an Accelerated Stock Buyback agreement (&#x201C;ASB agreement&#x201D;) with Goldman, Sachs &amp; Co. (&#x201C;Goldman&#x201D;) to repurchase an aggregate of $</font><font style="display: inline;">160.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of PMC common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company acquired these common shares as part of its $</font><font style="display: inline;">275.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million stock repurchase program announced on March 13, 2012. The aggregate number of shares ultimately purchased was determined based on the weighted-average share price of our common shares over a specified period of time.&nbsp;&nbsp;The contract was settled on October 5, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The total shares repurchased and cancelled under this ASB agreement was </font><font style="display: inline;">26,829,309</font><font style="display: inline;"> common shares at a price of $</font><font style="display: inline;">5.96</font><font style="display: inline;">. The repurchased shares were retired immediately upon delivery. Accordingly, the repurchased shares were recorded as a reduction of common stock, additional paid-in capital and accumulated deficit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">On November 10, 2011, the Board of Directors of the Company authorized a share repurchase plan for fiscal year 2012. Under this authorization, the Company may repurchase common stock to offset dilution from employee equity grants and stock purchases, at an aggregate cost not exceeding $</font><font style="display: inline;">40</font><font style="display: inline;"> million. As of December&nbsp;29, 2012, the Company completed its 2012 repurchase program and repurchased </font><font style="display: inline;">6,902,625</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares for approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">$40</font><font style="display: inline;"> million in cash.&nbsp;The repurchased shares were retired immediately. Accordingly, the repurchased shares were recorded as a reduction of common stock, additional paid-in capital and accumulated deficit.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">NOTE 13. EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">Post-Retirement Health Care and Pension Benefits</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company sponsors post-retirement health care for the benefit of United States employees and a defined benefit pension plan for the benefit of certain employees of its German subsidiary, all of which are legacy plans of previously acquired companies.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The unfunded post-retirement health care benefits provides retiree medical benefits to eligible United States employees who meet certain age and service requirements upon retirement from the Company. These benefits are provided from the date of retirement until the employee qualifies for Medicare coverage. </font>

The net period benefit expense was </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million during 2014 (2013 and 2012 - $nil). </font><font style="display: inline;">No</font><font style="display: inline;"> distributions were made from the plan during the period. The Company includes accrued benefit costs for its post-retirement program in Long-term obligations on the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Balance Sheet and recognizes changes in the accumulated post-retirement benefit obligation resulting from annual re-measurement in its results of operations.</font>

		<p style="margin:18pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Employee Retirement Savings Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company sponsors a 401(k) retirement plan for its employees in the United States and similar plans for its employees in Canada and other countries. Employees can contribute a percentage of their annual compensation to the plans, limited to maximum annual amounts set by local taxation authorities. The Company contributed </font><font style="display: inline;">$4.1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;">$4.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, and $</font><font style="display: inline;">3.9</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, and, to the plans in fiscal years 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:18pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Israeli Severance Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has </font><font style="display: inline;">two</font><font style="display: inline;"> types of severance agreements with employees in Israel, which are under Israeli labor laws. Under the first type of severance agreement, the Company&#x2019;s liability for severance pay is calculated pursuant to Israeli severance pay law. Severance is based on the most recent salary of the employee multiplied by the number of years of employment. The severance pay liability of the Company to these employees reflects the undiscounted amount of the liability. The liability is partly covered by insurance policies and by regular deposits to severance pay funds. The Company records changes in the severance liability in the Consolidated Statements of Operations, net of gains and losses related to amounts in the severance pay funds.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Under the second type of severance agreement, the Company&#x2019;s agreements with employees in Israel which are under Section&nbsp;14 of the Severance Pay Law, 1963. Under this agreement, the Company satisfies its full obligation by contributing one month of the employee&#x2019;s salary for each year of service into a fund managed by a third party. Neither the obligation, nor the amounts deposited on behalf of the employee for such obligation are recorded on the Consolidated Balance Sheet, as the Company is legally released from the obligation to the employees once the amounts have been deposited.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Expenses incurred related to the Israeli Severance Plans for 2014, 2013, and 2012 were </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.3</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, $</font><font style="display: inline;">1.6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, and $</font><font style="display: inline;">1.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively. The amount of the liability under the first type of agreement noted above is included within Long-term obligations on the Consolidated Balance Sheet in the amounts of </font><font style="display: inline;">$2.3 million</font><font style="display: inline;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;">3.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, as at December 27, 2014 and December&nbsp;28, 2013, respectively. The total amount of cumulative funding by the Company under the first type of agreement noted above are included within Investments and other assets on the Consolidated Balance Sheet in the amounts of </font><font style="display: inline;">$2.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">$3.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, as at December 27, 2014 and December 28, 2013, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company has been granted a tax holiday in Malaysia that has the effect of reducing its net income tax rate to </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">zero</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> in that jurisdiction. The Company&#x2019;s current income tax holiday was granted based on revenue, investment and staffing criteria targets to be met by PMC International Sdn. Bhd. (Malaysia). The tax holiday was granted in 2009 by the Malaysia Investment Development Authority and is effective through 2019, subject to continued compliance with the tax holiday&#x2019;s requirements. Tax savings associated with the Malaysia tax holidays were approximately </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$2.7</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million, </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$3.9</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million, and </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$7.9</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million in 2014, 2013, and 2012, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">consolidated</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> financial statements for the 2014, 2013 and 2012 include the tax effects associated with the sale of certain assets between our wholly-owned subsidiaries. GAAP requires the tax expense associated with gains on such intercompany transactions to be recognized over the estimated life of the related assets. Accordingly prepaid tax expense w</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">as</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> recorded in the years ended December 29, 2012, December 31, 2011 and December 26, 2010. The balance in prepaid expense to be recognized in future years was</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$0.1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, $5.8 million, and $19.2 million as of December 27, 2014, December 28, 2013, and December 29, 2012, respectively</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The provisions related to the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">income </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">tax accounting for stock-based compensation prohibit the recognition of a deferred tax asset for an excess benefit that has not yet been realized. As a result, the Company will only recognize an excess benefit from stock-based compensation in additional paid-in-capital if an incremental tax benefit is realized after all other tax attributes currently available have been utilized. In addition, the Company continued to elect to account for the indirect benefits of stock-based compensation such as the research and development tax credit through the consolidated statement of operations.</font>

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Company</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> determines its valuation allowance on deferred tax assets by considering both positive and negative evidence in order to ascertain whether it is more likely than not that deferred tax assets will be realized. The </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Company</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> records a valuation allowance to reduce the deferred tax assets to the amount that is more likely than not to be realized. Realization of deferred tax assets is dependent upon the generation of future taxable income, if any, the timing and amount of which are uncertain. Due to the history of losses the Company has incurred, the Company believes that it is not more likely than not all or a portion of the deferred tax assets held in the U.S., Canada and Israel will be realized.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The Company believes it is more likely than not that such assets will be realized to the extent presented on the balance sheet.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In 2014, the Company elected to release all </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">valuation allowance related to its PMC-Sierra Israel subs</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">idiary based on two consecutive years of </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">positive earnings</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">,</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> three years of cumulative positive earnings</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, and the subsidiary&#x2019;s forecast of continued profitability</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The release of valuation allowance </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">for the Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> Israel</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> subsidiary</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> resulted in a </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$6.9</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million benefit to the income tax provision in 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;For the year ended December 27, 2014, the Company decreased its total valuation allowance by </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$5.6</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, net</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">For the year ended December 28, 2013, the Company increased its valuation allowance by </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">$37.1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> million compared to the year ended December 29, 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;The increase was primarily due to the release of reserves on federal and state R&amp;D tax credits and the establishment of valuation allowance on foreign excess credits. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">In 2013 and 2012, the Company had approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">2.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and </font><font style="display: inline;">1.5</font><font style="display: inline;"> million stock-based awards, respectively, that were excluded from the computation of diluted net loss per share because they would be antidilutive.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">NOTE 1</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;IMPAIRMENT OF GOODWILL AND LONG-LIVED ASSETS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During fiscal year 2014 and 2013</font><font style="display: inline;"> the Company performed </font><font style="display: inline;">qualitative assessment for its</font><font style="display: inline;"> annual goodwill</font><font style="display: inline;"> and indefinite-lived intangible assets</font><font style="display: inline;"> impairment assessment for each of its reporting units and </font><font style="display: inline;">concluded that there is no impairment.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In the third quarter of 2012, the Company experienced weaker quarterly results and lower future projections than previously expected in its Fiber-to-the-Home (&#x201C;FTTH&#x201D;) and Wintegra reporting units.&nbsp;&nbsp;This was driven by slower</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">adoption rates of FTTH technology in markets outside of Asia and prolonged weak carrier spending whic</font><font style="display: inline;">h negatively impacted Wintegra.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">These circumstances triggered the Company to perform step one of the impairment test </font><font style="display: inline;">in the third quarter of 2012 </font><font style="display: inline;">and we determined that the estimated fair value of the reporting units was lower than their respective carrying values.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">T</font><font style="display: inline;">he fair values of these reporting units</font><font style="display: inline;"> in the third quarter of 2012</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">were estimated </font><font style="display: inline;">using a discounted cash flow model, or income approach.&nbsp;&nbsp;The discounted cash flows for each reporting unit were based on discrete financial forecasts developed by management for planning purposes. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Cash flows beyond the discrete forecasts were estimated using a terminal value calculation, which incorporated historical and forecasted financial trends for each identified reporting unit and </font><font style="display: inline;">considered terminal growth rates for </font><font style="display: inline;">other </font><font style="display: inline;">publicly traded companies</font><font style="display: inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Future cash flows were discounted to present value by incorporating appropriate present value techniques.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Specifically, the income approach valuations included the following assumptions</font><font style="display: inline;">, which were similar to those used in 2011</font><font style="display: inline;">:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 1pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-size:1pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse:collapse;width: 100.00%;margin-left:0pt;">
			<tr>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">ITEM&nbsp;9A.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">CO</font><a name="ControlsAndProcedures"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;">NTROLS AND PROCEDURES.</font>

		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Management, with the participation of our CEO and CFO, evaluated the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures pursuant to Rule 13a-15 under the Exchange Act, as of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report on Form 10-K. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Based on this evaluation, our CEO and CFO concluded that, as of December 27, 2014 our disclosure controls and procedures are designed at a reasonable assurance level and are effective to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed in our Exchange Act reports is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified by the SEC and that such information is accumulated and communicated to management, including our CEO and CFO, as appropriate, to allow for timely decisions regarding required disclosure. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:18pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Limitations on Effectiveness of Controls and Procedures</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In designing and evaluating disclosure controls and procedures, management recognizes that any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can only provide reasonable assurance of achieving the desired control objectives.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the design of disclosure controls and procedures must reflect the fact that there are resource constraints and that management is required to apply its judgment in evaluating the benefits of possible controls and procedures relative to their costs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:18pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Previously Reported Material Weakness</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">A material weakness is a deficiency, or a combination of deficiencies, in internal control over financial reporting, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of the Company's annual or interim financial statements will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In connection with a restatement of our financial statements in November 2013, filed on Form 10-K/A for the year ended December 29, 2012</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">and our assessment of internal control over financial reporting under Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 at December 28, 2013, </font><font style="display: inline;">manage</font><font style="display: inline;">ment, with the participation of our CEO and CFO, concluded that, because of an identified material weakness in our internal control over financial reporting relating to our accounting for income taxes, our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective at the reasonable assurance level as of December 29, 2012 and December 28, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Specifically, the Company did not have controls designed and in place to ensure the accuracy and completeness of financial information provided by third party tax advisors used in accounting for income taxes and the determination of uncertain tax positions, deferred income tax assets and liabilities and the related income tax provision and the review and evaluation of the application of generally accepted accounting principles relating to specific complex areas of accounting for income taxe</font><font style="display: inline;">s.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:18pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Management&#x2019;s Annual Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting,&nbsp;&nbsp;as defined in Rule 13a-15(f) and 15d -15(f) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 as amended.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting based on the framework in Internal Control-Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework).&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:18pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">We have focused on our internal controls over financial reporting for income taxes and haven taken steps to strengthen controls in response to the identified material weakness above.&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant internal control and process improvements were implemented in our tax accounting processes to enhance effectiveness and sustainability including:</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:24pt;"><p style="width:24pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;">
				<font style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:8pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>

			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt;margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Quarterly preparation of additional analysis related to the tracking and recognition of deferred tax assets, including excess tax benefits associated with stock option deductions, completed throughout 2014;</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:24pt;"><p style="width:24pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Hired senior level personnel with expertise in the area of tax accounting and reporting and engaged a new team of external advisors to assist with the Company&#x2019;s preparation and analysis of its income tax accounts;</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:24pt;"><p style="width:24pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:24.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Following the implementation of the changes in internal control over financial reporting described above, we conducted extensive evaluation of the effectiveness of the remediated tax accounting and control procedures.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on this evaluation, management concluded that the material weakness relating to our accounting for income taxes described above has been remediated, and management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 27, 2014 in providing reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&nbsp;&nbsp;The effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 27, 2014 has been audited by Ernst &amp; Young, LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, as stated in its report included in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">There were no changes in internal control over financial reporting, other than those described above, that occurred during the quarter ended December 27, 2014, that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</font>
